title: Representability and field base change for the scheme-theoretic centre
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All group schemes below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. The centre $Z(G)$ denotes the subgroup functor whose $A$-points commute with every element of $G(A')$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$. For every such $G$, this functor is represented by a closed normal commutative subgroup scheme $Z(G)\subseteq G$. For every field extension $K/k$, the natural equality $Z(G)_K=Z(G_K)$ holds as closed subgroup schemes of $G_K$.

source.place: Proposition 1.92 and the following paragraph, printed pp.33--34, taking the centralizer of the whole group.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Morphisms from any scheme $T$ to an affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are ring maps $R\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]; with the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] this identifies $G\times_kG$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kB)$, since $k$-algebra maps from the tensor product are precisely pairs of $k$-algebra maps. More generally $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_2=\operatorname{Spec}(R_1\otimes_RR_2)$. Since $B$ is finitely generated over $k$, generators $b_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes b_i$ generate $B\otimes_kB$; thus this product is affine of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The diagonal corresponds to the surjection $B\otimes_kB\to B$, $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$, so it is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This also proves that $G$ is separated, and the identical argument with $B\otimes_kB$ proves that the product is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Proposition 1.92, printed p.33, closedness of the diagonal; affine verification of its hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus] with $Y=G$, $S=G$, $X=G\times_kG$, $W=\Delta_G(G)$ and $f(h,g)=(h,ghg^{-1})$. Multiplication and inverse make this a morphism [def-sc-group-scheme]. Step 1 verifies the separated finite-type hypotheses and the closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow X$. We obtain a closed subscheme $L\hookrightarrow G$ such that a map $g:T\to G$ factors through $L$ exactly when $h\mapsto(h,ghg^{-1})$ on $G\times_kT$ factors through the diagonal, equivalently when conjugation by $g$ is the identity of $G\times_kT$.

source.place: Propositions 1.79 and 1.92, printed pp.30,33; Theorem 1.105, printed pp.37–38.

proof.text: For $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, equality of this conjugation morphism with the identity implies $ghg^{-1}=h$ for all $h\in G(A')$ and every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$. Conversely, these equalities apply to $A'=A\otimes_kB$ and the universal point of $G_A=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$. They say the conjugation morphism equals the identity on the universal point, so their coordinate-algebra maps agree [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Consequently $L(A)$ is exactly the centre functor in the statement, naturally in $A$. This uses all algebra points, not merely field-valued points.

source.place: Proposition 1.92 and following paragraph, printed pp.33–34; explicit universal-point verification.

proof.text: For every $A$, the identity lies in $L(A)$; if $z,w\in L(A)$, their images commute with every $h\in G(A')$ for every $A'$ over $A$, so $(zw)h=h(zw)$ and $z^{-1}h=hz^{-1}$. These identities make $L(A)$ a subgroup. In particular $zw=wz$ by taking $A'=A$ and $h=w$. For $g\in G(A)$, centrality gives $gzg^{-1}=z$, so the subgroup is normal. Thus the closed subscheme $L$ is a closed normal subgroup scheme by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Its multiplication is commutative by [def-sc-group-scheme]: evaluate it on the universal pair on the affine scheme $L\times_kL$, where the displayed commutation identity gives equality of the multiplication and its swap. Here $L$ is affine because it is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, hence is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Proposition 1.92, printed p.33, subgroup assertion; following paragraph, definition of the centre.

proof.text: Let $K/k$ be any field extension. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus], with $S'=G_K\to G$, gives $L_K=L\times_GG_K$ representing the same factorization condition for every $T\to G_K$. Writing $G_K=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=B\otimes_kK$ and $L=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I_0)$ (step 4), the affine fibre-product description of step 1 [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] gives $L_K=\operatorname{Spec}(C/I_0C)$, a closed subscheme of $G_K$. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], $G\times_kT=G_K\times_KT$ for a $K$-scheme $T$, and the pulled-back conjugation and diagonal are the conjugation and diagonal of $G_K$. For a $K$-algebra $A$, its $A$-algebra extensions carry the induced $K$-structure; hence step 3 identifies this condition exactly with $Z(G_K)(A)$. Equality is scheme-theoretic: two closed subschemes with the same factorization condition have ideals $I,J$ with $J\subseteq I$ by testing $C\to C/I$, and $I\subseteq J$ by testing $C\to C/J$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $L_K=Z(G_K)$ as closed subgroup schemes of $G_K$.
